quest.title: The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna
quest.description: Whether you're here to help Ruu or finish the commission, it's time to head to Tsurumi Island once more.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: This is the last possible location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu— We're here to help—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ruu—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What's that weird noise...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes! Monsters! Be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Kama? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the sky's looking all strange and stuff...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "This" Tsurumi Island is about to be destroyed. And then, everything will start again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's the thing that you talked about yesterday...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: However, it seems that things are even more serious than when I came here previously. Perhaps it's because you destroyed those perches...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: The name of the child you're trying to help... it's "Ruu," right?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: If we want to break the cycle and free Ruu, now is the time.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: That's why I'm here. To help.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did Miss Sumida ask you to do it?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: No, I've come here of my own accord.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? You're volunteering, Kama?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I don't know why either. I just feel like... I should be here. How should I describe that feeling... Ah. Right. It's like this.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "Perhaps I simply find it intolerably shameless for me to play the fly on the wall as you boldly step into Tsurumi Island."

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "Perhaps I believe that even illusions have feelings, and so I would do ill in allowing them to suffer in this cycle."

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "Or perhaps I simply think that I might help Ruu by breaking this perpetual ocean of fog, and in fulfilling the wishes of my ancestors I shall be freed from the 'history' that binds me."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Kama, since when were you...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Yes, Lady Sumida did speak these words. When I told her that I would like to help, she suddenly gained a spark of inspiration.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I did not understand what she said, but I believe that since Lady Sumida said so, then that must be how things are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds like her style alright...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon thinks yesterday's events have probably made Ruu too angry to talk to us...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I know. Lady Sumida said that "In this manner, the bloodline spanning millennia shall..."

choices.text: Could we lose the verbatim quotes?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: We shall. I believe that "Kama" — that is to say, I — can speak to him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's true that you do look just like the illusory Kama that we saw earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ruu did also mention that being unable to speak to those illusions weirded him out and worried him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So being able to talk to you should cheer him right up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, but where do we find Ruu...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, you're right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wakukau, Oina, and Autake... He did mention that these places wouldn't be hit by lightning under these circumstances.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And those would be his hiding spots where he'd wait out the storm.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well, let's go looking, then. Let's start with Wakukau Shoal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kama seems pretty enthusiastic today, eh...

choices.text: There's a few places the storm doesn't touch.
There is a very strong resemblance, yes.
Could we get to the point?
So much like a light novelist?
Those were Miss Sumida's words, weren't they...
You should probably leave this island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kama!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Were you about to say that the Thunderbird is dead or something?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: What? No! I was going to talk about a story that Lady Sumida told me.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Who do you take me for, seriously? How could I tell a child like Ruu such a thing?

choices.text: C'mon, Paimon, have a little faith.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon was just... Well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, enough already! So, about getting Ruu off Tsurumi Island...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He says that he can't leave this place...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps Tsurumi Island sustains his existence in some way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... If that's the case...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From what we've learned so far, the strange happenings on Tsurumi Island were caused by the Thunderbird destroying it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It feels like we can follow this line of reasoning to find a solution...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We could use the Thunderbird's feathers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon gets what you're trying to say, {NICKNAME}! If the state of Tsurumi Island now is due to ley line disorders caused by the Thunderbird's power...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then this feather, which also has that same power, might be able to sustain Ruu's existence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are we on the same page?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: You know what? I think you'd get along with Lady Sumida just fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Paimon's not sure if you're complimenting us or...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: She told me a story once, about a god of fertility who dwelt within the wheat fields, and who would travel afar with a human...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't wanna be mean or anything, but you're picking up her habit of going off topic, Kama...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But whatever the case, since we've decided what to do, let's just give it a try! It's better than nothing, after all!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Agreed. Well, if you don't mind, I shan't accompany you on this particular trip.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I'd like to take this opportunity to have a look at the place where my ancestors once stayed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But it's storming outside...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I know. I'll be fine, don't worry.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I mean, we live in Inazuma. Stormy days are our bread and butter.

choices.text: Not precisely, but let's go with your idea, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, of course!

choices.text: Um, let's leave that topic aside for now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, how are we going to get Ruu to Seirai Island, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: ...I thought Kapatcir had forgotten about all this...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I thought that this happened because she didn't approve of the ceremony. Because she didn't like me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You said that she was your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Friends don't forget their friends' words that easily!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's been waiting for you to sing for her all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yes, you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I did tell her that I would sing for her.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: But I haven't seen her in an awful long time now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Should we tell him? Y'know, that the Thunderbird was killed on Seirai Island...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, so, Ruu...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: The Thunderbird has—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: —Migrated to Seirai Island!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Y—Yeah, that's right! Didn't we tell you before that we saw this huge storm-cloud and a shattered mountain on Seirai Island?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's where the Thunderbird lives now! Y'know, we wanted to go up to Amakumo Peak to see the awesome face of the Great Thunderbird...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But the Thunderbird was super busy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, and she's had lots of baby thunderbirds too! They're all up in the clouds right now, though, and they don't come down much!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Baby thunderbirds...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So there's this vortex-like storm cloud over Seirai Island...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's formed by Kapatcir and the little thunderbirds as they play and fly in circles!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Wow, that's amazing! I mean, I've never seen it with my own eyes, but it already sounds unbelievably amazing!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Kapatcir must have been even mightier than I imagined!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And we did say before that we'd go outside on adventures together, didn't we?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #Yes, I remember. You did say that we'd go see other places, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Wanna go to Seirai Island together?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if she's busy and you can't see her...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Wow! Could I really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yup, we had an agreement, remember? {NICKNAME}'s not one to go back on {F#her}{M#his} word!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Awesome!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But I've tried leaving Tsurumi Island before, and I always end up back here again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Huh. That is a bit of a problem...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There has to be a way. Let's discuss the matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon would like to ask Kama some things as well! Hang on a sec, Ruu.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Alright!

choices.text: That's right. It was our agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. So the storm really doesn't reach this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon doesn't see Ruu anywhere either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where are you? We're here to help—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Looks like nobody's home.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Ahhhh—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, not like that! We're looking for something more like, "Ruu, it's Kama, where are you"!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Ruu, it's Kama, where are you—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still no response. Ohh, Paimon's getting worried...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, why is there no thunder or lightning here?

choices.text: Well, since it was the Thunderbird who destroyed Tsurumi Island...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! The "feather" from before!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, yeah, that's worth a try. Since Ruu said that it's one of the Thunderbird's feathers, we might get some reaction...

choices.text: We could try using the power of the "feather."

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready to go?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup! Anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well then, touch this Thunderbird feather first...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: For good luck? Sure!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: So, up there, that's...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! The Thunderbird... Kapatcir's up there in the sky.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's a little busy and can't come down to hear you sing. But if you do, Paimon's sure she'll hear you!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Mmhmm.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Actually, I know all about it. Or should I say I've guessed what happened to Kapatcir... and to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Ruu, we...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: No, it's alright. I'm so glad I got to know you! I mean, you even got me off Tsurumi Island to see the world outside!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: I could never have imagined that I could do this in the past. You're both really awesome!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: The clouds in the sky, the super special grass, and rocks up in the air. These were all Kapatcir's doing, right? She's so cool, too!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Even the air smells different. I mean, I'm not used to it, but it's amazing!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Well then, the weather's not the same anymore, but I've come to sing you a song, Kapatcir.

talks.objective: Touch the feather that suddenly appeared

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what's this? Looks like a feather...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Touch the feather)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, be careful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}! Hey, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was close. You were just frozen to the spot back there...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah, it's so beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: If only I could have seen such sights together with everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah, but I'm happy just to be able to do it with you two!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Still, the world beyond the fog is amazing! I never knew the sky was so high up or so large.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I wonder what the places Kama went to were like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can go see those places.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! The outside world is a reeeally big place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've met lots of interesting and nice people along the way, too. You'll hit it off with them in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's loads and loads of awesome food, too! Sweet Madames, Almond Tofu, Sticky Honey Roasts...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ooh! Sweet Madames sounds like they'll be great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right, we've had a ton of those in our journey, haven't we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, yeah! We also met a certain Tone-Deaf Bard during our journey. He loves music too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sure you two would be the best of friends. Maybe you'll even perform together in Mondstadt's city square!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And... And... We can take you on adventures! {NICKNAME}'s a real ace at that! We'll go to all sorts of places, like the super high-up Wangshu Inn...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup, I know, and I'd love to follow you all outside as well.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to you that I was able to fulfill my promise with Kapatcir. And... I guess everyone doesn't look all weird anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I thought that you'd broken the Perches, and I blamed you for that... Even though you're both good people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright! We've been on lots of adventures and got ourselves into a ton of misunderstandings. Don't take it to heart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And even if you don't wanna travel with us, we've got friends who'll take care of you! We know a young lady your age in Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Please leave Tsurumi Island with us, Ruu...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I... When we went to Seirai Island to sing for Kapatcir, I could feel that a piece of me was in that feather.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: That's why I'd like you to take that feather of hers on your travels.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: This way, I can travel with the two of you as well. We'll even bring Kapatcir with us, too!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: We'll go see the outside world, and we'll hear what songs they have to sing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup, you don't have to worry about me!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: It was great going outside, but it was real tiring, too...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'd like to rest for a bit. You can go on ahead first!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Oh, that's right! Could you please thank Big Brother Kama for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We will. See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup! Let's meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: We'll definitely meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it flew away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Paimon was worried sick, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems that I was drawn into the Thunderbird's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? The Thunderbird... The same one that destroyed Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, if that's the case...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It's just like Lady Sumida said. The will of the Thunderbird will resurface.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: In that case, the voice that we heard during the battle...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, Paimon heard it too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon's very curious now. It's almost like the Thunderbird was looking for someone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, that feather sure did bring about some kinda reaction, huh?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Yes, I saw you take out a strange feather earlier. Where did you get that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, this is how it went...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Huh. So the feathers of the Thunderbird were the basis for the Maushiro, and can summon spirits...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I was told these legends by my grandfather as he taught me how to make those Maushiro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so you can make 'em, huh! Then couldn't you just have made one for Lady... Err, Sumida?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well, because Lady Sumida did not ask. But if I should have the chance to help her in the future, I will mention this matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, what shall we do next? The direction in which the feather flew away doesn't quite match up with Oina Beach or Autake Plains...

choices.text: Tsurumi Island is in a lot of danger.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Yes, and we are on borrowed time as well. This will all start again once the thunder stops.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's forget about the feather's whereabouts for now. We've gotta get to the other spots where there's "no thunder" and look for Ruu there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then. Next stop, Oina Beach!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As long as we can talk to him, there's hope!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and Ruu said that things get real wild when the thunder starts coming down.

choices.text: There's no way to establish that at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...You know what? This story is even more bizarre than the plot of "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)."

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Also, stop calling me "Lady" this and "Lady" that already. You're an important friend of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Understood, Lady Sumida.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Oh, come on... Should I call you a pedant for the ages, or...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello there.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: #Oh my, oh my! It's the legendary {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: "And Paimon's the legendary Paimon!"

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Huh, funny. Shouldn't she make some retort at this juncture? This feels like we're departing from her character profile somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Character profile"?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Basically, that's what we call a combination of "image, traits, and history." Characters must adhere to the behavior prescribed in their profiles, or they will seem, well, out of character.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: S—Sorry...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: So, what about Ruu...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ruu says he's thankful to you.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Is that so? I see.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Wait, what happened? Why am I the only person who seems out of the loop here?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Ugh, never mind. Let's not stand around here. A change of scenery is in order, I think!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Sure. I'll pay. Consider this treat courtesy of a future contracted writer with Yae Publishing House and winner of the "This Novel is Amazing" grand prize!

choices.text: I agreed to take Paimon out for a good meal.
Have some consideration for the feelings of others, please.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Coming with you on your adventures is so awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Phew! I sure haven't sung in a long time. That was great!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'm sure Kapatcir heard me, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure she did.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Let's head back, then.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'd like to send this feather back to Kapatcir's home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This feather's just like the last one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Touch the feather)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Paimon will watch over you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've chased the monsters away—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Well then, anything you want to eat? Don't be shy, now!

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: You too, Kama! As for me, I'll start with a Tri-Flavored Skewer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, Paimon's full. Feeling much better now, too!

choices.text: You can have some more if you like.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you, Miss Sumida!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: It's no problem. I've been troubling you all this time, after all.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: The commission has been successfully completed. Indeed, I'd say the results far surpass my expectations...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I'd only wanted to get one Maushiro at first to use as reference for my writing.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But thanks to your perseverance, I not only got that, but also the story of the Sea of Fog, and of the millennia-spanning wait of a young lad on Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Mm... If my writing was better, this story would win me the "This Novel Is Amazing!" grand prize for sure!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But Kama's also changed quite a bit... I'd say these are all far more important than the completion of "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've also met some important friends...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't have a chance to travel with Ruu, but like he said, we'll definitely meet again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He'll keep his word.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! Paimon's sure he will. After all, he waited for so long just to keep his other promise!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, Miss Sumida, when will we get to read "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog"?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Uh, well, this...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I've decided to stop writing it for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what!? But we worked so hard to...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Ah, no, it's not an issue with you. Please don't misunderstand!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I wish to go traveling next.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: To gather more reference material?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I... I learned something very important during this commission.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: In the years prior to this, I lived only to create and write.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I learned fishing from Kujirai to write about a character who fishes for a living. His character profile was that of a masterful warrior who secluded himself in a fishing village and lived a peaceful life there, until...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Oh, right. Sorry... I almost went off-topic again. So, in order to better describe parties conducting illicit activities under a fictional national lock-down, Kama and I created a smuggling network that bypassed the Outlander Affairs Agency.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, it was mostly Kama's doing. And we discarded that work due to a writing bottleneck, which eventually resulted in the collapse of that network.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I've always been like this. I stopped fishing because I stopped writing that fisherman character. I went to apprentice at the Grand Narukami Shrine because I wanted to write about a shrine maiden's work...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But I understand now that I cannot just live, learn, travel, and adventure for the sake of writing novels.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I must live, learn, travel, adventure, and extract stories from there from which I shall write novels.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Kama was not born as the last son of Tsurumi Island for the sake of a story. Nor did Ruu stay in the Sea of Fog for so many years to be featured in a tale...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: And that's not why the two of you adventure and travel either, right? When I heard Miss Katheryne describe your adventures, I thought to myself...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: That you're just like the main character Kino in "Kino's Travels" and her companion "Hermos." The only difference is that no one has written your story. You are the story itself.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #A pair of outlanders who don't quite fit in anywhere, whose names are {NICKNAME} and Paimon! They stride across many strange lands and meet all sorts of people. They are drawn into all kinds of wicked plots and all manner of cruel wars. And each one of their adventures shall coalesce into shining gold...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: As Paimon has mentioned before, such a blurb would definitely suit you two.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: As such, aside from asking you two to help me gather reference material, I also wanted to understand you more — so that I might find the "seeds of a story" in the future.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: And I think I've found it. The seeds of a story are to be found in life and one's travels, and not in the character profiles, flowcharts, setting maps, and definitely not in things that you learn just to learn how to write them.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: As such, I've decided to stop writing and start traveling.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Until the time comes when the "story" begins to sprout... And then, I'll...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...Have an easy win in the "This Novel Is Amazing!" competition and become a writer contracted by Yae Publishing House!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Kama, will you come with me?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: We don't know where we're going, nor do we know when we'll return to Inazuma. We might even encounter many dangers. But that's exactly why I'd like you to stay by my side!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Of course, it's fine if you're not willing. I mean, everyone has their own lif{RUBY#[S]story}e to lea{RUBY#[S]tell}d.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I don't mind...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: No. That's not right... I'm more than willing. Let me come with you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Kama's... really changed...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: That's great! Then let's be off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? So suddenly?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, a real journey is one that's full of pleasant surprises and little accidents, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This... might be a bit too surprising... But still, please take care of yourselves!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: No worries! I'm sure we'll be alright no matter what happens so long as Kama's around.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Take care.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Thank you. Goodbye.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: If we should meet again, then let's do so where the sunset meets the sea. Then, I'll see if your soul, which shines so clearly like a diamond, has had any dust laid upon it or not.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #It's the famous closing lines of "The Vagabond Novice: Yamabuki Iro no Houroutan." Well then, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's part ways here.

choices.text: You... have a really impressive drive.
Make sure to thank Miss Sumida.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one flew away too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't look like Ruu's here either...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The feather's target seems to have been the mountain at the center of the island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kama, do you know anything about that mountain?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Mt. Kanna? It was where the Thunderbird reposed.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: That place is in fact a hollow cavern from which the Thunderbird would take off into the skies like a violet meteor that could be seen even through the fog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was said by the people of Tsurumi Island that the Thunderbird dispersed that mysterious fog to protect the island...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So you're saying...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (You relate the memories that came to you when you touched the feather.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That this fog wasn't created by the Thunderbird?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Huh. Perhaps our ancestors were wrong.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's understandable, considering that you can barely see the sun or the moon from down here. Maybe the Thunderbird's light was the only light they'd ever see.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Speaking of your ancestors...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's right. We saw someone who looked like an ancient version of you, Kama.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Here's what went down...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (You talk about "Sayo" and "Kama" from earlier.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...And that's what happened. They seemed to be pretty friendly with Ruu.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Hmm. That may truly have been my ancestor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, did the ancient Kama meet Sayo after leaving Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: The records don't say anything about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well, where shall we go next?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll keep looking for Ruu, of course! Let's see where the next spot is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We've been there before, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Paimon thinks we should go to the Autake Plains first...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh come on, let's focus on Tsurumi Island first! We should go to the Autake Plains next!

choices.text: That conflicts with what I saw in those memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah, it's so beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: If only I could have seen such sights together with everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah, but I'm happy just to be able to do it with you two!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: The world beyond the fog is amazing! I never knew the sky was so high up or so large.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I wonder what the places Kama went to were like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can go see those places.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! The outside world is a reeeally big place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've met lots of interesting and nice people along the way, too. You'll hit it off with them in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's loads and loads of awesome food, too! Sweet Madames, Almond Tofu, Sticky Honey Roasts...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ooh! Sweet Madames sounds like they'll be great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right, we've had a ton of those in our journey, haven't we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, yeah! We also met a certain Tone-Deaf Bard during our journey. He loves music too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sure you two would be the best of friends. Maybe you'll even perform together in Mondstadt's city square!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And... And... We can take you on adventures! {NICKNAME}'s a real ace at that! We'll go to all sorts of places, like the super high-up Wangshu Inn...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's also the Grand Narukami Shrine, which is way up high too, and has a big tree that looks like a kitsune! And we can go to Sangonomiya Shrine on Watatsumi Island. That place looks like something out of a dream...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup, I know, and I'd love to follow you all outside as well.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to you that I was able to fulfill my promise with Kapatcir. And... I guess everyone doesn't look all weird anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I thought that you'd broken the Perches, and I blamed you for that... Even though you're both good people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright! We've been on lots of adventures and got ourselves into a ton of misunderstandings. Don't take it to heart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And even if you don't wanna travel with us, we've got friends who'll take care of you! We know a young lady your age in Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Please leave Tsurumi Island with us, Ruu...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I... When we went to Seirai Island to sing for Kapatcir, I could feel that a piece of me was in that feather.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: That's why I'd like you to take that feather of hers on your travels.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: This way, I can travel with the two of you as well. We'll even bring Kapatcir with us, too!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: We'll go see the outside world, and we'll hear what songs they have to sing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup, you don't have to worry about me!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: It was great going outside, but it was real tiring, too...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'd like to rest for a bit. You can go on ahead first!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Oh, that's right! Could you please thank Big Brother Kama for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay. Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Yup! Let's meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: We'll definitely meet again!

talks.objective: Head to the designated location to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, didn't I tell you not to come here anymore...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's good to see that you're alright.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: But this place is super dangerous! There's thunder and lightning everywhere, and if you get struck by lightning, you'll get hurt! And I don't know why, but it looks like the storm's getting scarier than before...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: It must because you hurt that perch... Why did you come back... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu...

choices.text: We brought Kama to come see you.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Kama...?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "I'm back."

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Big Brother Kama... Is that really you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? Wait, are you an... illusion too, Kama?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Oh. Lady Sumida told me to say this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Come on, this isn't the time for tricks.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Oh. Sorry.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: The Kama you knew led a full life after leaving Tsurumi Island. His greatest regret was not being able to help you.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: #I'm a descendant of his. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and I are here to help you.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Descendant... Are you his son, then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm afraid you're quite a few generations off...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Wait, I don't get it. Descendants... Does that mean that Big Brother Kama is no longer around?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's been a long time, you know...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: What happened to him after he left?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: I waited for so, so long, until Tsurumi Island started looking like this, but he and Big Sister Sayo never returned. I've been so worried...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well, I do know a little about what happened to the Kama you knew. If you'd like to listen, I could tell you.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That'd be great!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: ...So many things happened in the outside world, huh...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: I never knew that the world beyond the fog was so big, or that it had so many people...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The unchanging nature of Tsurumi Island is the abnormal thing here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and that's why we're here to help!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Help...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But you destroyed the Perches and made Kapatcir angry...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: If the ceremony goes smoothly and she accepts me and our sacrifice, then everything will be fine again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That might not be what the Thunderbird wants...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #But how would you know, {NICKNAME}? You haven't met Kapatcir.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: She hasn't come back in so long. She must be angry...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't say this for sure, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmhmm. Let's give it a try.

dialogues.text: Curious tunes, tiny human. Afraid not of thunder and storms?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Eh...? Is this... the first time I met Kapatcir?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: The adults in the village all said that I can bring peace to thunder and storms.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this memory is clearer than before... Is that because Ruu is here?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: I was too embarrassed to sing in the village, so I came here to practice!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Do you like it? Hehe...

Before you humans learned to make fire, the thundering storm had already swept across the ocean alongside me. With but a flap of my wings, purple lightning will tear through the clouds like serpents. My cry shakes the ocean depths and heart of the earth.

I have heard the songs of the trees, the strains of the cloud and rain, and the melodies sung by the blue flying dragon of the far north. I have heard every trembling chorus of fox and rabbit and worm as I descended upon the land.
But your song is special. It is different from that of the boar, the fish, and the Wen Kamuy.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: You're speaking all funny. I don't get it...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: But I guess you like my song, then?
I do not know. I only know that I have never heard it before.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Well, then I shall sing you another tune — when you come again with thunder and rain!
Your lives are fragile and puny. Perhaps you shall already have turned to dust before I remember this matter. But if you have not, then you shall sing for me again.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Everything you say is so complicated...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Oh, yes! My name's Ruu. What's yours? Everyone in the village calls you "Great Thunderbird," but you must have a name, right?
A name?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Well, that is... What should I call you? I mean, if I want to sing for you again, and I call out to you, what shall I call out?
I do not know. She gave me a name long ago, but I have forgotten it. I do not need such things, nor have any dared to summon me thusly—

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Well, how about this then? Dad... I mean, Grandpa Mata taught me a few new words in the Ishine Script today. Let me try using them to give you a name!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Hmm... Oh! Oh, this should do!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: And so I gave her the name Kanna Kapatcir...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Let's name you "Kanna K{RUBY#[S]Great Eagle of the Storm}apatcir," then!

dialogues.speaker: Kapatcir
dialogues.text: ...Ridiculous. Still, it matters not to me.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Well, it's decided, then! I need to get back now, or the adults will worry. I'll definitely sing for you again!

dialogues.speaker: Kapatcir
dialogues.text: Hah. Perhaps I shall forget you immediately, "Ruu."

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Well, I won't forget! See you!

talks.objective: Talk to Ruu and the others at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it flew away...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: It flew off to Mt. Kanna...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Are those... Kapatcir's memories?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you did give her a name, after all.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: She also remembered my promise to sing for her again.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But... But if that's the case, why did everyone become like this? Why did the village become like this?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Did we anger Kapatcir by not performing the ceremony correctly?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't think that this was what the Thunderbird was mad about...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I see. I understand now, more or less.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well then, I suppose our next stop is Mt. Kanna.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But that's sacred ground. We can't set foot there...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #And {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you've already come around three times, and yet things haven't gotten better...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, you're the one who talked about "The Rule of Three."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Good omens must occur three times for good fortune to truly descend."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And "You must forge past obstacles three times to succeed on the fourth."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You know what? Paimon still thinks this should be called the "Rule of Four" instead!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: *sigh* Maybe you're right, Paimon...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: #True. You've already met with three difficulties, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That we have.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Alright. I believe you.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: And since Kama... I mean, Kama's descendant has also returned, this must mean that good things are in store for us...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But if nothing good happens, I'll be very, very mad, you hear?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Of course. Let's go, then.

talks.objective: Talk to Ruu and the others at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's finally over...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, Paimon really broke a sweat back there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh huh, and you were doing the fighting, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, Paimon's palms were getting all clammy watching you fight!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #Wow, I saw everything! That was so cool, {NICKNAME}! So cool!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: You truly were impressive. That was very eye-opening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon's still concerned about something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why... would there be this sort of monster here...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We fought one before back on Amakumo Peak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon remembers that one too, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We seem to be forgetting something important...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The "feather."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! That's right!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: What's this gotta do with feathers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So earlier, we took a commission from the Adventurers' Guild and went to Seirai Island to investigate...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: ...A talking cat?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Wow! A talking cat? Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that's... not the main point!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So while we were investigating Amakumo Peak, we defeated a monster just like this one, after which we got this special feather.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #Oh, so that's where you got your Thunderbird feather, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: That means that the Thunder Manifestations that appeared here and on Amakumo Peak must have something to do with the Thunderbird.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Sumida were here, she'd say something like...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Heh, funny.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: You don't look like you found it funny, Kama.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: No, no, I did find it quite amusing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Still, Paimon thinks that we've got a good picture of what's going on now, eh, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, we should go confirm our suspicions anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, Paimon thinks we've more or less got it already.

choices.text: I do this all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Kapatcir
dialogues.text: ...Since you have allowed this one and only song to flow in blood into this earth...

dialogues.speaker: Kapatcir
dialogues.text: Then until I, Kanna K{RUBY#[S]Great Eagle of the Storm}apatcir, hear that human... "Ruu"'s song once more, may these lands fall under an eternal catastrophe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what happened.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Huh, so that's what happened. And here I thought...

choices.text: It's a bit more extreme than I imagined...

talks.objective: Talk to Ruu at the designated location
Talk to Ruu at the designated location
Talk to Ruu at the designated location
Talk to Ruu at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Huh, how strange. I've only been away for a while, but it feels like it's been ages...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I'm back, and so is Kapatcir.

talks.objective: Talk to Ruu at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I can leave now, woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: So this is the heart of Tsurumi Island...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: I should bring Lady Sumida next time. I'm sure this sight would inspire her.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Everything's better now, and it's all thanks to you two. I... I'm truly blessed to have had the chance to call you both my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: How I wish I could join you on your journey.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: But... I'm really tired right now. I need to sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: So please go on ahead! I'll just be resting here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: We'll meet again someday for sure!
